title: Driving characteristics and their trade-offs
blurb: Which qualities this system actually optimises for, and what each one costs. Naming the tension is the point — 'token friction versus safety' is a choice, not an accident.

title: An auth decision, written as an ADR
blurb: Two options for how a browser extension authenticates to a backend, decided on coupling and connascence. Option A shares a cookie; Option B issues a scoped token. B was chosen, and the negative consequences are recorded alongside the positive ones.

title: STRIDE over a data-flow diagram
blurb: Four trust zones — your device, a third-party provider, my backend, model providers — with each STRIDE class mapped to the control that answers it. The interesting boundary is the one I do not own.

title: The domain as a state machine
blurb: Modelling the core of the product as explicit states and transitions rather than as procedures, so the rules live in one place instead of being spread across handlers.

title: How a change reaches production
blurb: A commit to a manifest, through reconciliation, to a running pod — including what happens when someone changes the cluster by hand instead. The drift is reverted, and that is the feature.

title: Platform topology
blurb: A single node running everything: GitOps reconciliation, secrets from Vault surfaced by external-secrets, SSO in front of each service, and deliberately vulnerable lab workloads isolated in their own namespaces. Network addresses are redacted here.

title: Fluency — container view
blurb: C4-style container diagram for the learning app: what runs, what stores state, and which boundaries carry authentication.

title: One review queue, two sources
blurb: Two independent card sources feeding a single scheduling spine. The design constraint was that a learner should never be asked which queue they are in.

title: Deck generation, with a control stage
blurb: A two-stage generation pipeline where the second stage exists to constrain the first. Generation without a control stage produces plausible cards that teach the wrong thing.

title: Reading companion — bookend retrieval
blurb: An overlay over a third-party reading platform that turns what you just read into scheduled recall, without persisting the licensed text. The trust boundary here is the one that matters.

title: Math rendering — the delimiter contract
blurb: As-is and to-be for math rendering, including an honest note that the fitness function meant to guard it is manual, tests the wrong renderer, and misses a real bug. Documenting a weak check is more useful than claiming a strong one.

title: Narration bake — serial versus pipelined
blurb: The same work done two ways, with the latency difference made explicit rather than asserted.

title: User flow — onboard once, then read
blurb: The whole product from the outside: one setup step, then a loop the user repeats without ceremony.

title: One round-trip, frontstage and backstage
blurb: A service-blueprint style sequence: what the user sees above the line, what the system does below it.

title: Integration layer — context view
blurb: A single adapter layer so several self-hosted apps can be driven through one interface. Designed, not deployed.

title: The abstraction that survives three APIs
blurb: Three services authenticate three different ways — a static bearer token, an exchanged JWT, an API key. The diagram works out what they genuinely share and refuses to abstract the rest.

title: Tool surface and least privilege
blurb: Every capability the layer would expose, scoped so that one compromised path cannot spend another service's credentials. Tokens stay server-side and never enter model context.

title: knowledge-drift — container view
blurb: A system for noticing when documented knowledge and reality have diverged. Designed against a written spec.

title: knowledge-drift — the governance loop
blurb: Who decides that something has drifted, and what authority the loop has to act on it.

title: Rift Bingo
blurb: A smaller, complete side project — included because a corrected architecture is more honest than an idealised one.
